title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 80 (Date of notice of charge)

content.overview: Where a charge on company property, assets or an undertaking is registered under section 77, a person acquiring that property, assets, undertaking, or any part, share or interest in it is deemed to have notice of the charge from the date of registration.
content.glance: Where a charge on company property, assets or an undertaking is registered under section 77, a person acquiring that property, assets, undertaking, or any part, share or interest in it is deemed to have notice of the charge from the date of registration.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 80 (Date of notice of charge). Where a charge on any property or assets of a company or any of its undertakings is registered under section 77, any person acquiring that property, assets or undertaking, or any part of it or any share or interest in it, is deemed to have notice of the charge from the date of registration. The rule depends on registration under section 77 and does not deem notice from an unregistered charge under this section alone. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Trigger
sections.body: A charge on company property, assets or an undertaking must be registered under section 77.

sections.heading: Persons and property covered
sections.body: Any person acquiring the property, assets or undertaking, or any part, share or interest in it, is deemed to have notice of the charge.

sections.heading: Effective date
sections.body: Deemed notice arises from the date the charge is registered under section 77.

provisions.title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 80: Date of notice of charge

examples.title: Constructive notice of charge
examples.body: Registration of a charge gives notice to persons dealing with the company of the facts recorded, from the date of registration.

hypotheticals.question: A purchaser acquires an interest in property subject to a charge that was registered under section 77. From when is the purchaser deemed to have notice under section 80?
hypotheticals.analysis: The purchaser is deemed to have notice from the date the charge was registered under section 77.

hypotheticals.question: Can section 80 itself deem notice of an unregistered charge?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 80's deemed-notice rule is triggered by registration under section 77; do not extend it to an unregistered charge under this section alone.

distinctions.title: Deemed notice and actual knowledge
distinctions.left: Section 80 deems notice of a charge from its registration date for a person acquiring covered property or an interest.
distinctions.right: Actual knowledge is a separate factual issue and is not the trigger stated in section 80.

misconceptions.trap: Treating deemed notice as arising before registration.
misconceptions.correction: Section 80 fixes the date of deemed notice at the date of registration under section 77.

misconceptions.trap: Applying section 80 to a charge without checking registration under section 77.
misconceptions.correction: The registered-charge trigger is an express condition of the deemed-notice rule.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 80 require?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Registration of a charge gives notice to persons dealing with the company of the facts recorded, from the date of registration.
